The bell tree is a percussion instrument in the tuned idiophone group, the gong-chime, xylophone and lithophone system, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.242.221. Some 14 to 28 inverted metal bowls are threaded vertically on an upright rod, roughly ordered by pitch and usually tuned to microtonal intervals. It is played by sliding a triangle beater, glockenspiel beater or xylophone beater down the tree to produce a glissando, which emphasises the beginning or end of a passage, creating a bright, glittering effect and adding complexity to the music. Chick Corea, Santana, America and Neil Peart of Rush, among others, have used it on recordings or in performance.

The player slides a triangle beater, glockenspiel beater or xylophone beater down the tree to make a glissando; the bowls are usually tuned to microtonal intervals rather than a formal scale, so the inexactness of the pitch order does not show in the glissando, which simply makes a fuller sound. The timbre is described as bright and glittering, and the instrument is often used to emphasise the beginning or end of a passage, adding complexity to the music.
